howItWorks.label: The process
howItWorks.title: Four steps —
howItWorks.description: Urban Utopia provides structure without constraining the creative process. Times are guidelines for a 45–90 minute session.

steps.title: Choose a location
steps.description: Upload a photo, use Street View, or pick an image from the workshop collection — the starting point is always the real place.

steps.title: Collect wishes
steps.description: Discuss as a group: What bothers you? What's missing? What does the group want? Ideas are captured directly in the tool.

steps.title: Generate a vision
steps.description: With objects, prompts, and AI, a visualization emerges — visible, discussable, comparable to the current state.

steps.title: Share & pass on
steps.description: Present results, gather feedback, and use them as input for school development, neighborhood planning, or political participation.

showcase.label: See it in action
showcase.title: From idea to
showcase.description: No stock photos as proof — instead, examples of how workshop ideas are translated into before-and-after images with Urban Utopia. Move the slider to see the difference.
showcase.ctaDescription: Jump straight into workshop mode — no setup, no fake data. Your first run often takes less than a class period.

projects.title: A safer route through the neighborhood
projects.description: More green space, wider sidewalks, less car traffic — typical wishes from participation workshops.

projects.title: A lively neighborhood square
projects.description: Visualization of a jointly developed idea for a lively meeting point in the neighborhood.

projects.title: A street for people
projects.description: Less asphalt, more trees and space to stay — reimagined together as a group.

projects.title: A new meeting place in the green
projects.description: An unused area becomes a place for encounter, play, and staying in the neighborhood.

testimonials.label: Voices from the field
testimonials.title: What teams value
testimonials.description: Anonymized feedback from workshops and pilot projects — without invented names or stock photos.

items.quote: Finally, participants don't just see that they're allowed to have a say — they see what their idea could look like. That changes the quality of the discussion.
What mattered to us was having results we could show in exhibitions and feedback to the administration — without extensive post-processing.
The technology stays in the background. The group remains the focus — and yet images emerge that people take seriously.

schule.title: School & education
schule.teaser: From project-based lessons to project days: students visualize the spaces they pass every day.
schule.heroSubtitle: Urban Utopia works for politics, geography, art, or interdisciplinary projects — across all grade levels.
challenges: Abstract topics like urban planning often feel far removed from students' everyday lives.
Discussions stay verbal — with no tangible outcome at the end of the lesson.
Results are hard to present or pass on within the school.
benefits: Location-based tasks: schoolyard, route to school, neighborhood.
Results as images — ideal for exhibitions, parent evenings, or school conferences.
No technical prior knowledge required; facilitation stays in your hands.

scenarios.title: Political education
scenarios.description: Experience democracy: Who decides about public space — and what could it look like differently?

scenarios.title: Geography & sustainability
scenarios.description: Discuss climate-friendly mobility, green spaces, and quality of stay at a specific location.

scenarios.title: Project week
scenarios.description: Several groups develop visions for the same place and compare their proposals.

schule.workshopTip: Plan for 60–90 minutes. Start with a short site visit or a photo — that creates shared reference points.

kommunen.title: Municipalities & administration
kommunen.teaser: Involve citizens, neighborhoods, and interest groups — with results that fit participation processes.
kommunen.heroSubtitle: For participation processes, community workshops, and municipal workshop series — from idea generation to documentation.
challenges: Minutes and mood reports alone rarely convince decision-makers.
Different age groups and perspectives need to come together in one format.
Results should be traceable and reusable.
benefits: Visualizations make wishes comparable — even for non-expert readers.
On-site workshops: marketplace, park, or street as the starting image.
Exportable images for reports, exhibitions, and online participation.

scenarios.title: Community workshop
scenarios.description: Open format in the neighborhood: participants develop visions together for a specific planning area.

scenarios.title: Process support
scenarios.description: Prepare workshop results as a supplement to online participation or professional planning.

scenarios.title: Youth & senior forums
scenarios.description: Different generations at the same place — different priorities become visible.

kommunen.workshopTip: Combine Urban Utopia with classic facilitation: first collect, then visualize, then prioritize.

planung.title: Planning & project development
planung.teaser: Early-phase workshops, studio reviews, and client presentations — when quickly understandable designs are needed.
planung.heroSubtitle: For planning offices, architects, and project developers who want to combine participation and design ideas in one tool.
challenges: In early phases, CAD visualizations are often still missing — yet images are needed for discussions.
Laypeople and expert audiences need to understand the same designs.
Iterations should be fast and possible without extensive rendering effort.
benefits: Quick variants from photos, Street View, or aerial perspectives.
Object library for typical elements: green space, mobility, places to stay.
Results as a basis for discussion — not as final planning evidence.

scenarios.title: Early phase & strategy
scenarios.description: Explore development options for vacant lots or neighborhoods with residents and stakeholders.

scenarios.title: Studio & teaching
scenarios.description: Students or teams compare design ideas at the same starting location.

scenarios.title: Client & investor meetings
scenarios.description: Visualize scenarios before expensive planning documents are produced.

planung.workshopTip: Use Urban Utopia deliberately as an ideation and communication tool — not as a substitute for professional planning.

vereine.title: Associations & initiatives
vereine.teaser: Neighborhood projects, citizen initiatives, and cultural formats — when people on the ground want to change something.
vereine.heroSubtitle: For associations, socio-cultural centers, and initiatives that want to think about spaces together and argue politically.
challenges: Good ideas often stay invisible when people only talk in circles.
When dealing with administration or politics, a convincing image is sometimes missing.
Volunteers need simple tools without a long learning curve.
benefits: Workshop in an afternoon — even without technical know-how.
Results for petitions, applications, social media, or local press.
Group work: compare several visions for the same place.

scenarios.title: Neighborhood festival & workshop
scenarios.description: Collect ideas on site and visualize them directly — as a highlight of the format.

scenarios.title: Initiative evening
scenarios.description: Prepare planned changes (green space, traffic, meeting places) for decision-makers.

scenarios.title: Cultural projects
scenarios.description: Combine artistic and participatory formats — space as a shared theme.

vereine.workshopTip: Invite different perspectives. Different images of the same place often open the most productive dialogue.

hochschule.title: University & research
hochschule.teaser: Seminars, studios, and research projects on cities, climate, and transformation — with reproducible workshop setups.
hochschule.heroTitle: Teaching and research with practical relevance
hochschule.heroSubtitle: Urban Utopia supports participatory formats in higher education — from field trips to transdisciplinary projects.
audience: Faculty in planning, geography, social sciences
challenges: Participation in teaching needs formats that fit within a semester.
Results should be usable both academically and for communication.
Different disciplines rarely speak the same visual language.
benefits: Reproducible process for seminars and multi-day workshops.
Documentation of group results for reports and posters.
Bridge between theory and concrete urban space.

scenarios.title: Seminar & field trip
scenarios.description: On-site analysis followed by visualization in the lecture hall or studio.

scenarios.title: Transdisciplinary project
scenarios.description: Students, practitioners, and civil society develop scenarios together.

scenarios.title: Research communication
scenarios.description: Prepare results for the public, municipalities, or funders.

hochschule.workshopTip: Define the study location and research question at the start — Urban Utopia structures the creative part.
